record.paper_title: String Theory on ADS3: Some Open Questions
record.context_brief: spin cutoff versus string spectrum and modular invariance
record.original_question: Can the proposed spin or mass cutoff k/2 ≤ j < 0, which may restore unitarity but removes the usual infinite tower of string excitations and gives a finite upper bound on the string level, be reconciled with the expected structure of string theory and with modular invariance of one-loop amplitudes?

evidence.quote: It is important to be aware that this latter possibility violates the generic structure of the string spectrum itself. We lose the infinite tower of string modes (the mass is cut off at the scale of the radius of ADS3), and consequently the hope of constructing a consistent spectrum shrinks. Modular invariance is expected to be spoiled.
As was already stressed, the consistency of a string with a finite number of mass levels is questionable. One can in particular wonder what the issue of modular invariance could be.
Once more, compatibility between unitarity and modular invariance appears as an important issue in understanding the string propagating over ADS3.

artifact.category_tag: AdS3 string spectrum and SL(2,R) WZW model
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider bosonic string theory on AdS_3 described by the SL(2,R) Wess-Zumino-Witten (WZW) model at level k > 2. The unitary continuous and discrete representations of the affine SL(2,R) algebra used in the spectrum are labelled by a Casimir parameter j, and a naive unitarity analysis suggests restricting j to the range k/2 ≤ j < 0 (so-called spin/mass cutoff). Imposing only this bound would: (i) cut off the worldsheet mass at the scale set by the AdS_3 radius, thereby eliminating the usual infinite tower of string excitations and producing a finite upper bound on the string oscillator level; and (ii) generically conflict with modular invariance of the one-loop torus partition function.

Problem: Construct a Hilbert space for strings on AdS_3 built from SL(2,R) WZW representations that simultaneously
  (a) is free of negative-norm states (no-ghost theorem),
  (b) preserves the infinite tower of string excitations characteristic of string theory, and
  (c) yields a modular-invariant one-loop partition function on the worldsheet torus.

In particular, determine whether the spin restriction k/2 ≤ j < 0 (or any refinement of it) can be reconciled with the expected stringy spectrum and with modular invariance of one-loop amplitudes, and exhibit explicitly the set of representations that must be included to achieve (a)-(c).
artifact.status_search_result: The question was essentially resolved by Maldacena and Ooguri (hep-th/0001053, hep-th/0005183). In Part 1 they showed that the correct Hilbert space requires augmenting the principal continuous and discrete representations with their spectrally-flowed images (parameterized by winding number w), with j restricted to 1/2 < j < (k-1)/2 in the discrete series; this preserves the infinite tower of string excitations and admits a no-ghost theorem. In Part 2 they verified that the one-loop partition function on thermal AdS_3 (Euclidean BTZ) is modular invariant and reproduces precisely this spectrum. Thus a naive cutoff k/2 ≤ j < 0 is not the correct prescription; the consistent resolution uses spectral flow.

status_evidence.title: Strings in AdS_3 and the SL(2,R) WZW Model. Part 1: The Spectrum
status_evidence.snippet: Studied classical solutions, spectral flow symmetry relating different winding numbers, and proved a no-ghost theorem for the representations involved.
status_evidence.claim: Provides a unitary stringy spectrum on AdS_3 using spectrally-flowed SL(2,R) representations, retaining an infinite tower of string excitations.

status_evidence.title: Strings in AdS_3 and the SL(2,R) WZW Model. Part 2: Euclidean Black Hole
status_evidence.snippet: The one-loop partition function on Euclidean BTZ / thermal AdS_3 is modular invariant with a spectrum consistent with that found in Part 1.
status_evidence.claim: Demonstrates modular invariance of the one-loop amplitude with the spectrum from Part 1, reconciling unitarity with modular invariance.
